summary: Return all subsets (the power set) of a list of distinct integers.
mainInsight: Every node of the include/skip decision tree is a subset: record the current path at every call, then extend it with each later element (start index) and backtrack. There are 2^n subsets.

approaches.name: Backtracking recording at every node
approaches.summary: Append path[:] on entry; loop over i >= start.

approaches.name: Iterative doubling
approaches.summary: For each element, add it to a copy of all existing subsets.

promptVariants: How many subsets does a set of n distinct elements have?
What does each recursive call record?
cards.explanation: Unlike permutations/combinations, the answer includes partial paths too. (2^n; the current path: every node is a subset)

incorrectOptionExplanations.C(n, k) only: That is combinations of one size.

promptVariants: Why is the answer recorded on entry rather than at a depth limit?
What does the start index do?
cards.answer: Every partial path is itself a valid subset, so each call appends a copy of the path immediately. The start index guarantees elements are added in increasing index order, so each subset is generated exactly once.
cards.explanation: The empty subset is recorded first.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Time complexity (copying each subset): ___
What is the auxiliary space excluding the output?
Besides the 2^n output subsets, what auxiliary space does subset backtracking use?
cards.answer: O(n): the recursion depth and the path.

promptVariants: What does the algorithm return for nums = [0]?
cards.explanation: The empty subset is always part of the power set.
